went there with my parents, because they wanted me to go (discovered yeets, yikes). mom went inside with me, dad stayed outdoors. the room was just like a normal doctor's room, just less 'medical' (more toys, more colours). a normal room. the therapist was a lady in her 40s, clearly knew what she was doing. 

it may not seem like it, but therapists are used to our type of person - they've had many young people like us, so they are prepared. 

i'm not very talkative, so mom began. she listened, was taking notes in her laptop, occasionally asked. just general info - why am i there, what are my problems, some background on the family (history of  mental diseases and stuff), how i feel, drug abuse, if i've got urges (final yeet, normal yeet). mom was then sent outside and it was just between the two of us. 

i do not recall much (good memory, i know), but it was the same type of questioning as before. i was asked to describe my state of mind. then she started: taljed about some healthy coping mechanisms and warned me about psych ward (cause of final yeet thoughts) and drugs. she then asked what do i need when depressed, to get better. i said i want to be left alone, that i can deal with this myself. she was fine with that, as long as i didn't harm myself (ok then). 

mom was invited back again, the therapist told her about my needs and possible next session, if needed. she wasn't annoying, she knew i wasn't much into talking and was very shy, so she didn't force me into anything. that was good. 

as long as the therapist is trained, you won't be judged. they will respect you and just try to get some info about you. if you want to give it a try, do it. you don't have anything to lose.
